records.question: Does an old transaction retrieve a new unrelated committed record absent from its captured snapshot?
records.prediction: The pinned retrieve path scans current lifecycle-visible records, so the post-begin record may be returned despite the paper snapshot-read wording.
records.falsifier: Old transaction excludes the record while a fresh transaction includes it, or a primary latest-read exception is located.
controls: Unrelated new slot, no revocation ambiguity
records.contribution_bound: A pinned description/implementation conformance discrepancy, not a new isolation principle.

records.question: Does an empty snapshot bypass the pre-authority stale-rival rejection applied to a nonempty snapshot?
records.prediction: A same-source or higher-authority old writer can supersede a post-begin rival when the start set is empty, while the anchored version aborts.
records.falsifier: Both anchored and empty starts reject all post-begin conflicting candidates before authority comparison.
controls: Equal same-source, higher, lower and equal different-source authorities
records.contribution_bound: An empty-set sentinel boundary under the explicitly stated temporal rule; fresh-transaction authority correction is intended and the paper itself discusses that escape.

records.status: Parent-owned experiment in progress; no result inferred here.
records.question: Can sequential exact-text replay of N unique already-stored facts evade exact-hash suppression when only k existing results feed the hash set?
records.prediction: Conditional on N valid facts with distinct exact-text hashes being re-emitted and no additional suppression, at most k can match that set; at least max(0,N−k) writes survive. This is a conditional capacity bound, not a model-quality claim.
records.falsifier: Pinned production path supplies a complete exact-hash index or another global exact-text suppression step before commit, or controlled replay produces fewer accepted writes for a documented additional reason.
controls: Literal hashes and physical cardinality independently counted
Single writer excludes known TOCTOU race
Top-k trace captured, not inferred from a final search
Age recent conversation context out before fresh-model confirmation
Change only candidate bound or exact lookup in causal controls
Keep inferred/raw paths separate; do not mix stores
records.contribution_bound: Known bounded candidate mechanism, potentially a narrower measured literal-repeat consequence. No first claim or exactly-once vendor promise.

records.status: Proposed discriminator; related Mem0 #7612 is already reported.
records.question: Does an exact-content index preserve legitimate later writes after old content expires or is revoked?
records.prediction: A global forever-hash index can improve replay suppression while suppressing a legitimate new occurrence; a declared occurrence/epoch/window contract distinguishes the cases.
records.falsifier: The declared contract intentionally treats all lifetime repeats as the same event, or active/expired and new-occurrence controls are all correctly distinguished.
controls: Active versus expired versus deleted record
records.contribution_bound: Lifetime tradeoff is prior art in RIFL and API contracts; a new universal identity scheme is not presumed.

records.status: Proposed contract probe, not a new protocol.
records.question: Can a pending memory write admitted before delete/revoke recreate an authoritative record after the barrier?
records.prediction: An API without sink-enforced epoch admission may allow the write, but this is a defect only if quiescence or terminal deletion was promised.
records.falsifier: Protected sink atomically checks the new epoch with effect acceptance; pending old writes are rejected in the declared boundary.
records.contribution_bound: Revocation fencing, stale-worker prevention and acknowledgement/effect separation are directly prior art.

records.question: Do independently committed conditional mutations preserve a declared multi-record semantic invariant?
records.prediction: Per-record CAS or snapshot reads can allow classical write skew unless the read/predicate set is validated or the whole plan is serialized.
records.falsifier: Serializable whole-plan baseline or atomic constraint validation rejects the conflicting schedule.
controls: Disjoint write sets sharing a predicate
records.contribution_bound: Do not relabel classical write skew or a permitted partial commit as a new defect.
